svg.text: THE PARADE'S CLOCK
a service yard by day, a street of discharges by night
MICKEY'S CARS
Quay Street, the Hook
ART PROPOSAL for ruling 6. Not canon.
Times are AUTHORED and hang on two sourced facts and one studio ruling, all three named on the sheet.

THE DAY BEFORE IT
propped doors, crates on the pavement, and nobody queueing
A man in waders washes the cinema steps and the
pavement under the canopy with a hose and a yard
brush. The water runs to the channel and the street
is wet before it rains.
Tivoli
The bill-poster pastes the hall's wall: four sheets,
a bucket, and last month's bill going up in strips.
the Institute Hall
Potatoes to the chip shop, in hessian sacks off a
flat-bed, through a propped-open front door because
there is no back way in.
Coley's
The poster change at the cinema. Two cases open,
glass leaning against the wall, and for twenty
minutes anybody can see what is coming.
Tivoli
The launderette's service call: a man with a toolbox
and a machine pulled out from the wall.
the Bright Spot
Cash collection from the amusements, in a bag, by
two men, at the same time every week. THE STREET'S
ONE PIECE OF DAYLIGHT INFORMATION WORTH HAVING.
the Penny Rooms
The all-night cafe changes shift and the night man
goes home past the queue for nothing.
the Anchor Cafe
Deliveries stop. The crates come in off the pavement
and the doors that were propped open all morning are
shut one by one.
everywhere
AND THE NIGHT
three discharges, and everything else absorbs them
The early house goes in. The queue is short and mostly
couples.
Tivoli
+30 min
The chip shop opens its second fryer. Steam on the inside of
the glass from here until it shuts.
Coley's
+45 min
The main feature. THE QUEUE IS AT ITS LONGEST AND THE STREET
IS AT ITS EMPTIEST.
Tivoli
+15 min
The video shop's last hour. Friday, a queue at the counter;
Tuesday, one man and the door bell.
the video shop
+60 min
The music room's support act finishes and the doorway fills
with people who came outside to smoke.
the Institute Hall
+30 min
THE LAST BUS. Whoever is not on it is walking or ringing.
the stop outside the Tivoli
+20 min
THE CINEMA TURNS OUT. Two hundred people on a wet pavement in
ninety seconds.
Tivoli
+2 min
The chip shop queue reaches the poster case. The phone box has
three people at it and one of them is holding the door open
with a foot.
Coley's, the box
+8 min
The cab telephone on the wall is in constant use and there is
an argument about whose car is whose.
the wall telephone, the rank
+30 min
The music room turns out. Smaller, louder, and it goes on down
the coast road.
the Institute Hall
+45 min
The all-night cafe is the only lit window with people in it.
Drivers, two nurses off shift, and a man who is not going
anywhere.
the Anchor Cafe
+165 min
The street belongs to the gulls and the man who washes the
cinema steps.
everywhere
WHAT THE CLOCK IS BUILT ON
SOURCED: bus deregulation from 26 October 1986 thinned evening and
Sunday services across the country, sourced by this project on
2026-09-08. SOURCED: the first British multiplex opened on 23
November 1985 with ten screens and took over a million admissions in
its first year, and admissions had bottomed at 54 million in 1984
across 1,246 screens, which is what the Tivoli is shabby because of.
SOURCED: the Entertainments (Increased Penalties) Act 1990 received
Royal Assent on 13 July 1990 and raised the penalties for unlicensed
parties, which is the period's own nightlife story and has nothing
to do with drink. RULED: the studio decided on 2026-09-09 that the
last bus out of Meridian goes about half past ten, because the walk
home through a dark port town is where the game happens.
AND THIS IS THE CONSEQUENCE
After 22.30 every person on this street either walks home through a dark port town or finds a
telephone. There are exactly two telephones on the Parade: the public box, which the project already
owns as E3_telephone_kiosk, and a direct line in a steel hood screwed to the wall between the cinema
and the chip shop, with no dial on it, which rings one office. THE ATLAS PUT A TAXI LANDLINE NOTICE
ON THIS STREET BEFORE ANYBODY PROPOSED A CAB OFFICE.
